text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.59% today as oil prices climbed back toward $100 a barrel, driven by escalating U.S.-Iran tensions in the Persian Gulf. Reports of Iranian attacks on U.S. Navy ships and the broader risk of supply disruptions from Middle East conflict have kept crude elevated—U.S. oil is now at $91.48, up sharply from earlier in the week. The stock's 5% gain over two weeks tracks directly with this oil price recovery, since ConocoPhillips profits when crude prices rise.

Beyond today's headline tensions, wealthy investors are actively competing to snap up oil and gas assets precisely because this conflict-driven price environment is expected to persist. With political figures suggesting energy prices won't ease until after the midterm elections, the outlook for sustained higher oil prices is supporting valuations across the sector.
